newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end unchanged, crown softer.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end unchanged, crown softer.

text.p: 1415 GMT - Swedish bond yields closed unchanged on Thursday after a day of quiet trade but the crown weakened against both the mark and the dollar.

On Friday market players will eye the U.S. and Germany as no statistics are expected, dealers said. * Six-month T-bill rate falls one basis point to 4.13 pct. * Ten-year bond yield flat at 7.17 pct. * Crown softens to 4.4700 to mark vs 4.4585 late on Wednesday.
Swedish bond yields closed unchanged on Thursday after coming off morning lows in quiet trade and the crown softened against both the mark and the dollar.
Market players ignored a Philadelphia Fed Survey that brought U.S. yields some basis points lower, dealers said.
"The movement in the U.S. was too small for us to act on," a trader said. "Trade has been extremly calm today."
The six-month T-bill rate slipped one basis point to 4.13 percent, while the ten-year bond yield ended flat at 7.17 percent.
The crown weakened to 4.4700 against the mark from 4.4585 crowns late on Wednesday, but trade was quiet.
"The dollar weakened a bit when Tietmeyer said he did not mind a strong mark," a dealer said.
"The crown also weakened but at 4.47 crowns to the mark we saw some interest in selling marks for crowns."
Market players are expected to focus on currency movements and the debt markets in the U.S. and Germany on Friday as no important figures are due out.
